# tfcensus

> Count what your Terraform manages: units, states and the AWS resources no unit manages.

## Start

- [Getting started](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/getting-started): A first read-only run of tfcensus: check the setup with doctor, list units, read their state with inventory, and find unmanaged AWS resources with scan.
- [Install](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/install): Install tfcensus from a release archive, with mise or with go install, verify the release signature, and install the man pages and completion scripts.
- [Supported versions](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/supported-versions): The terragrunt, terraform and OpenTofu versions tfcensus runs with, the features that need newer ones, and the state versions it reads.

## Guides

- [Choose accounts](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/accounts): Pick the AWS accounts tfcensus reads: profiles and globs, an AWS Organization with one role or a role per OU, accounts.map for odd profile names, and include and exclude lists.
- [Speed up scans with the aggregator](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/aggregator): Make scan faster across many accounts: read AWS Config through an organization aggregator, turn on Resource Explorer views, and narrow layers, types and regions.
- [Find unmanaged resources](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/scan): Find the AWS resources no Terraform or OpenTofu state manages, find out why one landed in its category, and fail a CI job on unmanaged or double-managed resources.
- [Write and test ownership rules](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/rules): Write an ownership rule for resources that are unmanaged on purpose, test it offline with rules test, and keep it honest with reasons, expiry dates, guards and never_hide.
- [Audit state backends](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/audit): Check state buckets, lock tables and the fleet of states with audit backend, set the policy thresholds, suppress accepted findings with a reason and an expiry date, and gate CI on severity.
- [Check drift in CI](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/drift-ci): Check drift on a schedule and on pull requests with tfcensus-action, upload SARIF to code scanning and keep one drift comment per pull request.
- [Hide drift noise](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/drift-noise): Hide drift you have decided to live with, such as tags_all updates and computed hashes, with drift.noise presets and rules that carry a reason and an expiry date.
- [Find who manages an ARN](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/whois): Find which units and state addresses manage an AWS ARN or ID, check a batch from a file or a scan report, and answer offline from a saved state index.
- [Adopt resources with codify](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/codify): Turn the unmanaged findings of a scan report into import blocks for one unit, pick findings by type or CEL expression, and generate the config with terraform plan.
- [Move resources between units](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/move): Move resources between Terragrunt units with tfcensus move. Draft the file from plans, verify it, apply it, roll back from S3 object versions, or use the native strategy.
- [Publish reports with notify](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/notify): Send drift, unmanaged resources and backend audit findings to Slack, GitHub issues, a GitHub or Bitbucket pull request comment, or files with tfcensus notify.
- [Build the HTML report](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/html-report): Turn saved scan, drift and audit JSON into one self-contained HTML file with tfcensus report html, with a coverage trend from several scans.
- [Use tfcensus from an MCP client](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/mcp): Register tfcensus mcp in Claude Code or another MCP client, give it saved reports, and ask about units, unmanaged resources, whois, audit findings and drift.
- [Add an AI summary to CI](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/ai-summary): Add an opt-in job to the drift workflow that sends the drift report to a model your organization picks and appends its answer to the job summary.
- [Read OpenTofu encrypted state](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/encrypted-state): Read OpenTofu states that use client-side encryption with --decrypt-with-tofu, which runs tofu init and tofu show -json in each unit with the unit's own key configuration.
- [Emulators and proxies](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/endpoints): Point tfcensus at an AWS emulator with AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, and run it behind an HTTPS proxy or a TLS-inspecting proxy with its own CA certificate.
- [Shell completion](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/guides/completion): Set up tab completion for tfcensus in bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell, nushell, elvish, xonsh, tcsh, oil and clink, and debug it when it offers nothing.

## Concepts

- [Read-only by default](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/safety): What tfcensus reads, the three commands that write, why it prints identifiers and never state values, and what reaches child processes, agents and models.
- [Units, repos and workspaces](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/units): How tfcensus finds Terragrunt units and plain Terraform root modules, how it resolves each one's state backend and target account, and when it runs terragrunt render.
- [How state is read](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/state): How tfcensus reads Terraform and OpenTofu state from S3 backends, with which credentials, without a lock, and what each read status means.
- [Inventory layers](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/inventory-layers): The sources a scan lists live AWS resources from, which one wins when two report the same resource, and how to see the blind spots with --explain-coverage.
- [Matching](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/matching): How scan and whois join a live AWS resource to a resource in state, by identity, then ARN, then normalized ID, and why an unmapped type is undetermined instead of managed.
- [Scan categories](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/categories): The eight categories a scan puts each live AWS resource in, how a child resource takes its parent's category, and how the coverage percentage is counted.
- [Ownership rules model](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/rules): How ownership rules decide who owns a resource no state manages, with built-in packs, your own CEL rules, guards and never_hide, where the first rule that matches wins.
- [Terragrunt and terraform](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/terragrunt): Which terragrunt, terraform and tofu commands tfcensus runs, which environment variables reach them, how it reads TFCENSUS_* variables, and how logs and Ctrl-C work.
- [Caches](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/caches): The probe and scan caches tfcensus keeps, what they hold, how long they stay fresh, which commands read them, and how to inspect or clear them.
- [Why there is no built-in LLM](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/concepts/no-llm): Why tfcensus makes no call to a language model, and the two ways to use one with its reports anyway, an MCP agent or an opt-in CI job, with you choosing the provider.

## Reference

- [Configuration](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/config): Every tfcensus config key with its type, default, environment variable and flag.
- [Environment variables](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/environment): The environment variables tfcensus reads, and the ones it passes to child processes.
- [Exit codes](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/exit-codes): What each tfcensus exit code means, and which commands return it.
- [Output formats](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/output): The output formats of each tfcensus command, the --out flag, and the JSON envelope that every --format json output shares.
- [Fail-on values](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/fail-on): The --fail-on values of each tfcensus command, which make it exit 3.
- [JSON schemas](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/schemas): The JSON schemas of tfcensus's config file and JSON output, with the URL each is served at.
- [Ownership rule packs](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/rule-packs): Every rule of the built-in ownership packs and the guards: what each matches, the category it sets and why.
- [CEL fields and functions](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/cel): The fields and functions an ownership rule's match expression can use, with the CEL syntax for tags, attributes and related resources.
- [Matching and rule IDs](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/rule-ids): Every rule ID a scan, whois or drift finding can carry, with the category it sets and what it means.
- [Type mapping coverage](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/type-coverage): Which Terraform resource types tfcensus maps to a CloudFormation type, which inventory layer lists each, and which types stay undetermined.
- [Backend audit checks](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/audit-checks): Every check of tfcensus audit backend with its severity, what passes and how to fix a finding.
- [Drift noise presets](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/drift-noise): The built-in drift noise rules, what each hides and the drift.noise entry that turns it on.
- [Move file format](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/move-file): The migration file that tfcensus move runs, every attribute of a migration block, the address and action syntax, the history object, and the findings that reject a block.
- [MCP tools and prompts](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/mcp): The tools and prompts that tfcensus mcp serves, with their input schemas.
- [IAM policies](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/reference/iam): The read-only IAM policy for every tfcensus command except move apply, rollback and mark-applied, what each statement is for, and the permissions of the move commands.
- [Changelog](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/changelog): What changed in each tfcensus release, from the release notes that release-please writes.

## CLI

- [tfcensus](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/): Take a census of Terraform/OpenTofu and Terragrunt fleets on AWS
- [Global flags](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/global-flags): Flags that every tfcensus command accepts.
- [tfcensus audit](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/audit/): Audit state backends
- [tfcensus audit backend](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/audit/backend): Check state buckets, lock tables and the fleet of states
- [tfcensus cache](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/cache/): Inspect or clear the probe and scan caches
- [tfcensus cache clear](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/cache/clear): Delete every entry of both caches
- [tfcensus cache info](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/cache/info): Show each cache's directory, entry count, size and freshness
- [tfcensus codify](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/codify): Write import blocks for unmanaged resources from a scan report
- [tfcensus completion](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/completion): Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
- [tfcensus config](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/config/): Inspect and validate configuration
- [tfcensus config init](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/config/init): Write a commented config file
- [tfcensus config path](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/config/path): Print the config file locations tfcensus reads
- [tfcensus config show](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/config/show): Print the effective configuration
- [tfcensus config validate](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/config/validate): Validate config files against the schema
- [tfcensus doctor](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/doctor): Check tool versions, AWS credentials and the inventory layers of each account and region
- [tfcensus drift](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/drift): Find drift between the units' state and AWS
- [tfcensus inventory](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/inventory): Read each unit's state: versions, providers, resource counts, serial and lineage
- [tfcensus mcp](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/mcp): Serve units, inventory, whois, scan_summary, audit_findings and drift_summary to an MCP client over stdio
- [tfcensus move](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/): Move resources between the states of Terragrunt units
- [tfcensus move apply](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/apply): Apply a migration file to the units' states
- [tfcensus move mark-applied](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/mark-applied): Record migration blocks as applied without changing state
- [tfcensus move plan](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/plan): Verify a migration file with plans, without writing anything
- [tfcensus move rollback](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/rollback): Restore the states a migration file changed
- [tfcensus move status](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/status): Show whether each migration block is applied in each unit
- [tfcensus move suggest](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/move/suggest): Draft a migration file from the moves that plans show
- [tfcensus notify](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/notify): Publish saved scan, drift and audit reports to Slack, GitHub, Bitbucket or files
- [tfcensus report](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/): Render saved scan, drift, audit and index files without collecting again
- [tfcensus report audit](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/audit): List the findings of a saved backend audit, highest severity first
- [tfcensus report drift](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/drift): Summarize a saved drift run: unit statuses and drifted resources
- [tfcensus report html](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/html): Write a static HTML report from scan, drift and audit JSON
- [tfcensus report inventory](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/inventory): Count the managed resources of a saved state index per unit and type
- [tfcensus report scan](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/scan): Summarize a saved scan: counts and the top unmanaged resources
- [tfcensus report units](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/report/units): List the units of a saved state index
- [tfcensus rules](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/rules/): Work with ownership rules
- [tfcensus rules test](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/rules/test): Compile ownership rules and evaluate them against sample resources, offline
- [tfcensus scan](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/scan): Find AWS resources that no unit manages
- [tfcensus units](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/units): List units with their state backend, target account and region
- [tfcensus version](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/version): Print version and build information
- [tfcensus whois](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/cli/whois): Show which units manage an AWS resource

## Help

- [Troubleshooting](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/troubleshooting): Fixes for common tfcensus failures, from expired credentials and unreadable states to scan false positives, a move that stopped halfway and notify errors.
- [FAQ](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/faq): Short answers about what tfcensus changes, which tools and backends it needs, how it treats secrets, and how it fits into CI and agents.
- [Scan accuracy](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/accuracy): How often scan calls a resource unmanaged when something else owns it, measured on three real non-production AWS accounts, with aggregate counts only.
- [Security and verification](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/security): How to report a vulnerability in tfcensus, how to verify a release's signature and provenance, and where the third-party license notices are.
- [Contributing](https://tfcensus.sasskovacs.dev/contributing): How to build and test tfcensus from source, the checks a pull request must pass, and how to work on this docs site.
